entries.claim: The closer the chord is from the center of the circle, the longer its length is and vice versa.
entries.quote: The closer the chord is from the center of the circle, the longer

entries.claim: Theorem: If chords of a circle are equal in length, then they are equidistant from the center.
entries.quote: If chords of a circle are equal in length, then thay are equidistant from the center.
entries.note: Theorem is stated on page in yellow box, matching the claim exactly (with minor typo correction)

entries.claim: Corollary: In congruent circles, chords which are equal in length are equidistant from the centers.
entries.quote: In congruent circles, chords which are equal in length, are equidistant from the centers
entries.note: Corollary is stated on page in orange box, matching the claim exactly (with minor punctuation difference)

entries.claim: Converse of the theorem: In the same circle (or in congruent circles) chords which are equidistant from the center(s) are equal in length.
entries.quote: chords which are equidistant from the center (s) are equal in length
entries.note: The claim is explicitly stated in the highlighted 'Converse of the theorem' box on page 61. The exact quote appears verbatim in the yellow highlighted section.
